title: Canonical qcqs strict-local comparison for module coefficients
statement: Let Λ be a commutative coefficient ring, f:X→Y a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], s:Spec Ω→Y a geometric point with Ω algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], and F a sheaf of Λ-modules on X_et [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Write R=O^sh_(Y,s) and ρ:Spec R→Y for the affine pointed-neighbourhood colimit and its structural map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit; def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map], Z=X×_Y Spec R, p:Z→X, H=p⁻¹F. For each small-model affine pointed representative (V,v), let c_V:Spec R→V be the canonical limit leg followed by Spec Γ(V,⊤)≅V. The map Z→V×_Y X has components (h c_V,p), where h:Z→Spec R. Its graph gives the terminal-neighbourhood morphism δ_V from Z to p⁻¹(V×_Y X). Define r_V:F(V×_Y X)→Γ(Z,H) to be the p-adjunction unit at V×_Y X, restriction along δ_V, and the inverse terminal-section identification. This is implemented by qcqsStrictLocalNeighbourhoodSection and qcqsStrictLocalSectionRestriction, using pullback symmetry to match the library's reversed orientation. There is an isomorphism e:(f_*F)_s≅Γ(Z,H) such that germ_(V,v) followed by e.hom equals r_V for every affine pointed representative. The predicate IsQcqsStrictLocalModuleComparison is exactly these equations. Stalks and germs use pointSmallEtale.sheafFiber and toPresheafFiber [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. This asserts continuity and its representative formula; it says nothing about exchange or restriction to a geometric fibre.

proof.text: Refinement compatibility makes the specified linear restriction maps a cocone over the small affine pointed-neighbourhood diagram.

Initiality of the affine pointed-neighbourhood inclusion makes the whiskered module stalk cocone a colimit. Its desc to the restriction cocone constructs a linear map; the colimit fac equation gives every required germ equation.
The invertibility theorem for a given map with those germ equations supplies IsIso. Apply asIso; its hom is the constructed map, so its representative formula is unchanged.

12 hits including presheafFiber_hom_ext, toPresheafFiber_naturality, toPresheafFiber_w, and toPresheafFiber_presheafFiberDesc. These are general colimit tools, not the desired etale comparison or exchange identity.
